title: empirical-fidelity-sampler-int8-4bit-fp8-sheet
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, empirical sampler for mapping quality vs cost vs latency across INT8 / FP8 / 4-bit (and mixed) quant modes for a set of production workloads. The goal is to produce actionable guardrails and numeric thresholds that can be dropped into the Optimize heuristics and the deployment recommender (console).

Scope and audience:
- Intended for product/optimize engineers and applied-ml to run quick batch experiments and capture representative sample points.
- NOT a final econometric model; this is a sampling layer used to populate distributions used by the heuristics engine.

High-level approach (how to use the sheet):
1) Pick a workload slice (e.g., "chat-short", "completion-long", "embedding-search-64") and upload or paste N sample requests (N=100-500 recommended).
2) For each sample, run baseline FP32/FP16, then run each quant mode (INT8, FP8, 4-bit) with the same prompt/seed and record outputs and timings.
3) Compute per-sample quality metrics (e.g., embedding cosine with baseline, BLEU/ROUGE proxy for completions, perplexity delta for language-model-likelihood tasks).
4) Aggregate by percentile (p50/p90/p99) for latency and quality drop; compute per-token cost using per-mode GPU throughput multipliers.
5) Feed aggregated points to the Recommender as (latency_ms, quality_delta, cost_per_1M_tokens) tuples.

Sheet layout (columns to include):
- sample_id  (string)
- workload_tag  (string)  e.g. chat-short, embed-64
- seq_len  (number)  tokens in request + expected response
- baseline_mode  (string)  fp16
- baseline_latency_ms  (number)
- baseline_quality_score  (number)  e.g., embedding cosine with reference
- quant_mode  (string)  int8 | fp8 | 4bit | mixed-int8-4bit
- quant_latency_ms  (number)
- quant_quality_score  (number)
- quality_drop_pct  (formula) = (baseline_quality_score - quant_quality_score) / baseline_quality_score * 100
- qps_measured  (number)
- throughput_multiplier (user-provided or measured) e.g. 2.2x for int8
- cost_per_token_mode  (formula) = baseline_cost_per_token / throughput_multiplier
- est_cost_per_1M_tokens  (formula) = cost_per_token_mode * 1e6
- fallback_recommendation (string)  e.g. fallback-to-fp16-if-drop>2% OR fallback-to-int8-for-non-critical
- notes (string)  free text: GPU type, kernel variant, quant library, date/time

Key formulas (write them into the sheet as plain formulas where possible):
- quality_drop_pct = IF(baseline_quality_score=0, "NA", (baseline_quality_score - quant_quality_score) / ABS(baseline_quality_score) * 100)
- cost_per_token_mode = baseline_cost_per_token / throughput_multiplier
- est_cost_per_1M_tokens = cost_per_token_mode * 1000000
- latency_regret = quant_latency_ms - baseline_latency_ms
- effective_throughput = 1000 / quant_latency_ms * batch_size  (approx when single-threaded)

Default parameters / recommended measurement knobs:
- sample size: 200 samples per workload_tag (min 50 for exploratory)
- seq_len buckets: [<64, 64-256, 256-1024, >1024]  (report results per bucket)
- batch sizes for throughput tests: 1, 4, 8, 16 (only run small batches if SLOs require low latency)
- GPUs note: record hardware label (A100-80GB, H100, L4) and CUDA/cuDNN/oneAPI runtime versions
- baseline_cost_per_token: use internal cost that maps to current cloud spot/reserved GPU hourly rates — record source

Example row (illustrative):
- sample_id: s0001_workflowA
- workload_tag: chat-short
- seq_len: 64
- baseline_mode: fp16
- baseline_latency_ms: 45
- baseline_quality_score: 0.982 (embedding cosine)
- quant_mode: int8
- quant_latency_ms: 28
- quant_quality_score: 0.973
- quality_drop_pct: 0.92%
- qps_measured: 35
- throughput_multiplier: 1.5
- cost_per_token_mode: (baseline_cost_per_token / 1.5)
- est_cost_per_1M_tokens: computed
- fallback_recommendation: "allow-int8 but fallback-to-fp16-if-drop>1.5% for embed-search"

Aggregation and output buckets to populate the recommender service:
- For each (workload_tag, seq_len_bucket, quant_mode) produce: p50_latency_ms, p90_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, p50_quality_drop_pct, p90_quality_drop_pct, p99_quality_drop_pct, median_cost_per_1M_tokens.
- Export format: CSV with header: workload_tag,seq_len_bucket,quant_mode,pXX_latency_ms,pXX_quality_drop_pct,median_cost_per_1M_tokens

Suggested rollout heuristics (starter rules):
- If p90_quality_drop_pct <= 1% AND p90_latency_ms <= baseline_p90_latency_ms * 0.9 -> recommend quant_mode for production (low-risk).
- If p90_quality_drop_pct between 1% and 3% -> recommend canary for non-critical routes with automatic rollback if quality-regression alerts fire.
- If p90_quality_drop_pct > 3% -> DO NOT recommend for sensitive workloads; consider mixed-precision (int8 encoder + fp16 decoder) or per-request quant switching.
- Add cost-savings threshold: require >= 20% estimated cost reduction vs baseline for any production recommendation unless explicitly approved by product.

Measurement pitfalls and gotchas (notes to copy into experiments runbook):
- Kernel variability: int8/4bit kernels often show more variance at cold-start; capture warm-up runs separately and use warm samples (drop first 10-20 runs).
- RNG/decoding nondeterminism: for completion quality metrics, fix seeds or use deterministic sampling (greedy/beam) when possible to measure fidelity.
- Calibration shifts: some workloads (LLM summaries) are more sensitive to tail-cases; embedding cosine average can hide tail regressions — always check p99 of similarity.
- Mixed quant setups: record layer-splits and whether KV cache is preserved; these materially change latency/cost math.

Open questions / TODOs:
- TODO: add small helper script to compute throughput_multiplier from raw traces (Ethan to pick up).
- TODO: formalize baseline_cost_per_token mapping to Dedicated vs Hosted pricing (Priya to own mapping table).
- Open question: how to represent perceived quality for generative tasks beyond simple numeric proxies (UX-labeled buckets? human eval sample?). Propose small 100-example human eval for 2 representative workloads.

Quick experiment plan (next 2 weeks):
- Week 1: run sampler for 3 workloads: embed-64, chat-short (avg seq 64), completion-long (avg seq 512) on H100 + A100. Produce CSV exports.
- Week 2: run canary group (select customers) with auto-fallback if p90-quality-drop>1.5% over 24h. Capture request-level traces.

Notes & provenance (keep this short):

- Derived from earlier quant exploration docs but re-focused on an empirical sampling layer intended to provide distributions to the recommender rather than a deterministic decision matrix.
- See linked artifacts for experiment logs and PRs.
